localeFormatting.note: is-IS and en-US disagree on both separators and date order. Every case below is the same value rendered two ways, and in each pair the en-US rendering is a plausible-looking wrong answer rather than an obvious error. This is why locale assertions must compare formatted strings against an is-IS expectation, never against a number.

numbers.trap: the group separator and the decimal separator are swapped between the two locales
reading 1,5 as fifteen hundred is a four-order-of-magnitude error
the is-IS form reads like a large whole number, which is how a fractional krona survives review

dates.trap: both are valid dates in both locales — 4 September or 9 April, and nothing on screen says which
for any day of the month up to 12 the two readings are indistinguishable
days above 12 are the only ones that give the mistake away, which is why the bug ships

payDate.rule: Wages land on the 4th of the month following the pay period.
